stem:
Esha looks at the diagram. Straight line $ROS$ passes through $O$, and ray $OT$ cuts the straight angle into adjacent angles $\angle ROT$ and $\angle TOS$. The marked angle $\angle ROT$ is $55^{\circ}$.

Which claim correctly finds $\angle TOS$?

options.text: $\angle TOS=180^{\circ}$, the measure of the whole straight angle at $O$.
$\angle TOS=180^{\circ}-55^{\circ}=125^{\circ}$, because the adjacent parts of the straight angle add to $180^{\circ}$.
$\angle TOS=55^{\circ}$, matching the printed degree mark on $\angle ROT$.

teacher.key_rationale: Adjacent angles on straight line ROS sum to 180°, so ∠TOS=180−55=125. Naming only the whole, copying 55, or using a right-angle complement all miss that split.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle as straight line ROS with ray OT and marked adjacent angle 55°.
